links.reason: 1825 says only that they will seize the herds (இனநிரை கோடும்) and meet him in the field; that his answer to niraikol is a known trait they plan on rests on the marker's nuance, not the Tamil. 454 is a real earlier herd recovery, so the callback is plausible but thin.
Line 4 துன்பம் தாங்கி இன்பமென் றிருத்தல் அரிது matches the couplet's இன்னாமை இன்பம் எனக்கொளின். The verse adds that the very act the Kural rewards is hard, which is a real qualification.

355 is the sumantiri's report that austerity (நோற்று) ends all evil; Tirumanthiram 258's கேடில் புகழோன் விளைக்கும் தவமறம் can as easily mean the renowned doer's austerity and virtue as a god who makes them fruitful. The grace-versus-effort dispute is imposed, not stated.

Both verses show Civakan circling a Jina's shrine (வலங்கொண்டு), but 2743 ends in praise and says nothing of teaching; the 'last circling that leads to a teaching' is supplied from the plot. It is a recurrence in story order, not an answer or fulfilment.

2427 says only that the whisk-waving guards are beyond count (தொகை யென்பதின்றி); it makes no claim about kingship. 27 states the renunciation, but no incompatible claims are set against each other, so this is irony imported from the patikam.

செய்த வம்புரியாச் சிறியார்போல் is a simile for her helplessness (உய்யல் ஆவதொர் வாயில்); it is not an account of why the man she wants is out of reach, and Kural 270 is about want and wealth. The shared word is non-penance, and the gains clauses over-read it.

Both make taking another life as one's own the basis of not killing (ஒருயிர் போல நெஞ்சத் துருகி / தன்னுயிர்போல் எண்ணி). That is agreement rather than development, though the pairing does show the Jain vow-base and the Siddhar's tapas wish side by side.

156 gives the mourners' doubt (சிறப்புடை மரண மில்லை) and 139 has the king refuse to kill even for his life (என்னுயிர் நீத்த வேனும்). The scene does refute their view, but the mourners' words are reported, not answered in the text, so the link leans on the reader's reconstruction.

286 names the poison plot (நஞ்சின் துஞ்சும் வகை சூழ்ந்து) and her fall into hell; 292 has poison forced down her (நஞ்சுண மடுத்தார்). The punishment mirrors the crime and the later verse fulfils the earlier.
36 shows ministers speaking of Udayana's merits, but nothing in it shows Pradyota's anger or a plot; the claim that the truth ends in a plot is reconstructed. The verse is flagged uncertain.

In Akananuru 152 வல்லினும் வல்லார் ஆயினும் சென்றோர்க்கு ... நிறைய வீசும் describes the kandhal flower's scent wafting for all who pass, not Aay giving elephants; and the Aay is not shown to be Andiran by name alone. The note misreads line 19-21.

Both verses voice a measured life-span (வாழ்நா ளுலந்ததேல் / வாழும் நாளும் அளந்தன). That Sitattan alone survives and Saccandan dies is not in these verses, so the contrasting uses are supplied from outside.

8 says the lesser demons search because their god's refuge was removed (கடவுள் புகனீக்குதல்); 45 has them complain to Neelakesi that the sage forbade the bali and flesh offering (பலியும் ஊட்டுதல் பாவம்). 45 supplies the content of the earlier phrase.

14 says he gave nectar to the dying dog (அமிர்து ஈந்த) but does not say the dog is repaid by a god; that comes from 15. The pair mainly shows a timely gift, which Kural 102 praises, so it is illustration.

Both make a woman the face of Death (கூற்றமே என்றிட்டால் / கூற்றென்பதனை ... பெண்டகையால்). The conceit is shared and the pairing shows it, but the epic does not limit or condition the couplet, so same_image fits better.
1784 shows silent worship at the Jina's feet (வாமனடிக் கேற்றி) but nothing of her grief; the persistence of suffering is drawn from the next verse, outside this link.

599 has the king sleepless over whether guarding will fail (காவல் ஓவுங்கொல் என்று கண்படான்), which illustrates Kural 549's வேந்தன் தொழில். The felt cost is a small addition and the epic side does not lack a rule, since line 2 states kings are the life of the people.

1801 recalls the burning-ground birth (புறங்காட்டுள் ... வீழ்ந்தேன் துணையாகித் தோன்றினாய்) that 309 describes with ghosts and owls and her question whether this is how kings are born. The recall reverses her lament into thanks for the companion.

Both prefaces use the moon's spot for the poet's flaw: 4 asks the learned to wash the மறு with wit, 6 says even the moon is not spotless and he will own any fault. The shared use is the same modesty topos placed in different hands.

The note rests on a commentator's reading that the 'others' in 661 are army, fort and friends; the Tamil says only மற்றைய எல்லாம் பிற. 661 is about firmness in action, 381 about a king's six assets, so the pairing is a thin theme.

326 makes killing (கொன்ற தீவினை) lead to sorrow, animal births and hell, while Kural 255 ties hell to eating flesh. The 'old rule that links it to killing for food' is not in 326, so the gains over-read.

166 shows a former king as a timid peacock in the palace; 'his son's house' is not in the verse, and the Naladiyar's fall (வீழ்வர் ... மனையாளை மாற்றார் கொள) is loss to enemies, which hints at no afterlife.

290 contrasts the thief's lost footing with the non-thief's keeping the gods' world; it does not give two punishments, this world and the next. 2870 does give royal torture and a fallen birth, so the pairing is real but the claim exceeds the couplet.

105 shows the astrologer speaking to display his learning (புலமை தன்னைக் காட்டுதல்), which does not assert astrology's worth; Naladiyar 52 calls the prattlers of சோதிடம் foolish compared with those who reflect on impermanence. That is a difference of priority, not incompatible claims.
This is two stages of one festival in order; the verses make no claim that the later one answers or fulfils the earlier. 1075 is corrupt and cryptic, and the shared day is read in.

116 says they will prepare the stone platform and post a guard for the day the astrologer named (மொழிந்த நாளினால்), answering 108's prediction of a messenger with a letter in Pushpakarandam. The later unit responds to the earlier.

1003 paints her நாட்டமும் நடுக்கமும் as she stood terrified before the elephant; 976 shows that trembling (மின்னுப்போல் நுடங்கி நின்றாள்). The portrait fixes the moment of fear, though 'ground of the love' is an interpretation.

In 640 the kings would turn to great penance (நற்றவம் செய்குவம்) only if they lose her; it is not a means to win her, so it does not take penance on the couplet's motive. The 'next verse' it cites is outside the link.
Both verses show a prince mastering a rutting elephant, but the motif is stock; neither verse shows a captive or a captor's trust, and 98's elephant kneels in homage while 67 is a street display.
46's மதமடக்கிச் செலுத்திடுவான் foretells curbing an elephant's rut, and 57 has him subdue the maddened elephant (நாகத்தை அடக்கிக் கொண்டு). The later verse fulfils the sage's sign.
links.text_issue: 46: marked reading says curb pride, but மதம் is rut

links.reason: Both use the cloud and elephant comparison, but 880 has elephants taking thunder for a rival and 951 has the clouds and young elephants hard to tell apart. The pairing shows a stock conceit; it does not show a mistake moving from beasts to the poet.

44 says austerity cuts away the heated deeds (வெம்பிய வினை அறுத்து); Naladiyar 51 says the same with a warning on exhausted merit. The idea that the prophecy needs the prince's lasting effort is not stated in 44.

1280 has the astrologer declare the bite hard to cure even for the Lord (பகவற்கு மரிது தீர்த்தல்); in 1290 the venom leaves at his gaze (நஞ்சு நீங்கிற்று). A claim and the scene that refutes it; the healer's learning is in other verses.

668 says no one can bar fate (விதியினை விலக்க மாட்டா), which agrees with Kural 380 and adds no condition; the king's giving way and the hero's rejection are outside the verse. The speaker is not shown to be the king.

179 has the doors burst open as he circles; 185 has him shut them after the praise. This is the same visit in story order, and the note's lesson that the praise lies between is a structural observation, not a development.

1695 repeats 23's simile (வெண்மதி இழந்த மீன்போல் / மதியம் கெடுத்த வயமீன்) and has the brother arrive at the bright city, so the fulfilment is real. But 1695 names no woman, so identifying her as Gandharvadattai is not from the verse.
1079 has the king order Civakan seized and his strength rooted out (ஆண்டிறங் களைவென்), which could illustrate excess, but the elephant, the usurper's envy and the later fall are outside the verse.

15 says a god came down like lightning (மழை மின் என வந்த ஓர் தேவன்) and carried him from prison; 1156 shows him sensing it with his left eye and knowing by ஓதி the plight of உயிரனானை. The verse fills out the patikam's line; 1156 ends with his rising to the sky, not the descent.

523 has the envoy rebuke the king (எள்ளியோ ருரையும் ஈயாது இருந்தனை), which departs from Kural 685's brief, smiling speech. But the verse makes no claim about how envoys should speak, so this is a norm broken, not a tension.

1389 runs பேதைமை to வினை, வேட்கை and மரணம், and Manimekalai 109-124 gives the nidana chain from ஊறு to பற்று and துன்பம். The shared causal shape is real, but the Cintamani tree is not a limit on the chain, and the teaches sentence mostly states the common theme.
446 calls the youth மடங்கலை அடுந்திறல் நெடுந்தகை's foe, and 772 shows the lion killed (மா விதனைக் கொன்றாய்) so that the world sleeps in peace. The later verse shows the deed that earns the title.

Both use அவல்தொறும் with the toads' call and கார்தொடங் கின்றே/கின்றால் காலை, and the speakers read the same signs as despair in 364 and as the chariot's coming in 453. The link shows same words and different belief; 'qualifies' does not fit, and 364 does not open with the frogs.

2549 has the women speak desire and beg with their eyes (காமஞ்செப்பிக் கண்ணினா லிரப்பார்), but nothing shows he has not answered, so the one-sided begging is read in. The pair is a thin contrast with the couplet's words made useless by the eyes' agreement.
